html:
Michif Piyii is the Michif name for the homeland of the Métis, a people of mixed First Nations and European descent who formed in the fur trade country of the Canadian prairies and the North-West. The map shows the homeland as it is claimed today; the Métis themselves arose only in the late 1700s, from the families of French Canadian and Scottish fur traders and Cree, Ojibwe and other women.

Their heartland was the Red River settlement, now Winnipeg. They were famous bison hunters and freighters with Red River carts, and worked for the Hudson's Bay Company and its rivals. Their language, Michif, mixes Cree verbs with French nouns.

When Canada took over Rupert's Land in 1869, Louis Riel led the Red River Resistance, which led to the creation of Manitoba in 1870. A second rising in Saskatchewan in 1885, the North-West Resistance, was crushed and Riel was hanged. Canada's constitution of 1982 names the Métis as one of its three Aboriginal peoples.
